rounds.text: Aditya Birla Capital Ltd displays robust long-term growth fundamentals, underscored by a 10-year compounded sales growth rate of 29% and a 5-year compounded profit growth rate of 28% [E14, E19]. The intrinsic valuation highlights significant undervaluation, with a discounted cash flow model placing intrinsic value at Rs 684 per share against a market price of Rs 402, offering a substantial 41.2% margin of safety [E39, E40]. Furthermore, a reverse DCF indicates that the current share price only prices in a modest 10.7% earnings growth, which sits well below the 18.0% growth assumed in the base case [E41]. Momentum confirms institutional backing and price strength, with domestic institutions increasing their stake by 4.91 percentage points since December 2023, positive overall institutional money flow, and the stock trading comfortably above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E37, E38, E44]. Rules-based screening supports this positive outlook, scoring the company 78 out of 100 with a BUY recommendation driven by strong trailing twelve-month profit growth of 33% and year-over-year net profit increases [E21, E58, E59]. Conceded: [E4], [E29], [E32], [E55].

Aditya Birla Capital Ltd carries severe underlying balance sheet vulnerabilities and a cash generation profile that directly contradicts its headline optical multiples. Most alarmingly, operating cash flow and free cash flow collapsed to extreme negative figures of Rs -36,544 Cr and Rs -36,905 Cr respectively in March 2026, driving an abysmal cash conversion ratio of -9.46x against reported profit [E29, E30, E31]. Furthermore, leverage risks are glaringly high with a debt-to-equity ratio of 4.43x where non-current liabilities exceed equity capital, alongside a perilous current ratio of just 0.09x indicating current liabilities vastly outstrip current assets [E32, E33]. Valuation premiums also lack fundamental backing, with the stock trading at a P/E of 23.93x and an EV/EBITDA of 15.29x—both exceeding their respective sector benchmarks of 18.8x and 12.83x—while simultaneously offering a 0.00% dividend yield and suffering from a negative 3-year compounded profit growth of -7% [E4, E6, E11, E20]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong long-term compounded sales growth of 29% over 10 years, a high institutional domestic backing increase, and a positive 12-month price return [E14, E37, E46]. Nevertheless, decelerating earnings growth signals, low interest coverage, and a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -83.1% underline that the current valuation carries severe downside risks [E47, E56, E63].

Conceded: operating cash flow and free cash flow reached extreme negative figures of Rs -36,544 Cr and Rs -36,905 Cr with a cash conversion of -9.46x [E29, E30, E31], leverage stands at 4.43x non-current liabilities to equity [E32], and the current ratio is 0.09x [E33]. However, these balance sheet figures coexist with robust fundamental momentum, including a 10-year compounded sales growth of 29% and a trailing twelve-month profit growth of 33% [E14, E21]. Although the P/E of 23.93x and EV/EBITDA of 15.29x exceed sector benchmarks [E6, E11], the company delivers a strong 10.35% ROE compared to a sector benchmark of 5.27% [E9], alongside a rules-based screen score of 78 out of 100 pointing to a buy [E58]. Conceded: dividend yield is 0.00% [E4], 3-year profit growth is -7% [E20], and historical drawdown reached -83.1% [E47]. Nevertheless, domestic institutional backing has increased by 4.91 percentage points, and institutional money flow registers as positive [E37, E38], supported by a rising EPS trend and a 41% YoY net profit increase [E59, E62] that signal underlying operational expansion well beyond optical multiples.

Conceded: 10-year compounded sales growth is 29% and TTM profit growth is 33% [E14, E21], and domestic institutions increased holdings by 4.91 percentage points [E37]. However, this top-line expansion obscures a severe 3-year profit contraction of -7% [E20] and a pattern of decelerating earnings growth [E63]. While the bull points to a 10.35% ROE beating the sector benchmark [E9], filed statements reveal a low historical return on equity of 12.5% over the last 3 years [E57] and a low interest coverage ratio [E56]. Furthermore, the impressive short-term profit metrics coexist with catastrophic cash burn, evidenced by an operating cash flow of Rs -36,544 Cr and a cash conversion ratio of -9.46x [E29, E30]. This aggressive growth valuation of 2.58x book value [E54] and a 0.00% dividend yield [E4] relies on earnings that fail to translate into cash while carrying a heavy 4.43x leverage ratio [E32] and an alarming -83.1% historical peak-to-trough drawdown [E47].
